thread:
darius (AE): Kicking off POC coordination with Convex — they want latency & throughput validation before signing. Primary asks: sustained 300 qps with 99th p50 < 150ms for small chat model, plus cold-starts and burst to 1k qps. Also have a brief security questionnaire. Can we run a mixed workload profile next week?
elaine (SE): Yep. Proposed plan: smoke on Tue, sustained ramp Wed (30m at 300 qps), 1h stress with bursts Thu. Need region (us-west-2) and a model variant — suggest gpt-j-emu-13b-quant for cost, fallback to gpt-j-emu-6b for tail.
chris (SRE): For the stress run I need the exact prompt size distribution. Small chat = 32-64 tokens output, avg input ~40 tokens. Any embeddings or rerank calls mixed in?
darius (AE): Convex will do chat + occasional embedding (1 in 50). We'll surface embeddings separately but include a 2% embedding mix in the run.
elaine (SE): Good — I'll craft the load profile. Example locust snippet we plan to run:
```
# simplified
POST /v1/generate
payload = {"model":"gpt-j-emu-13b-quant","input":"<sample>","max_tokens":64}
```
We'll use 300 concurrent users ramping to target qps with latency histogram export.
chris (SRE): Two infra notes: 1) reserve Dedicated pool for the run or we risk noisy neighbors; 2) KV cache warmup matters — schedule a 10m warm phase before measuring.
darius (AE): Pricing question from Convex: want run-time estimate for hosted vs. dedicated for sustained 300 qps over 1h. Also curious about burst pricing to 1k qps for 10min.
elaine (SE): Rough numbers: hosted per-token estimate ~ $0.00075 per token (13b-quant), expected token burn ~ 40 in + 50 out avg = 90 tokens -> ~$0.0675 per call. At 300 qps for 1h that's 1,080,000 calls -> ~$73k (hosted). Dedicated reserved capacity with a 1-month commit would be far cheaper per-token; I'll send a formal calc.
darius (AE): Oof — please double-check. Convex will push back on hosted cost.
chris (SRE): For Dedicated we can provide a throughput estimate: 3 x A100-equivalent instances in pool should handle 300 qps for 13b-quant with headroom. I'll include expected tail-latency numbers.
olivia (Security): On questionnaire: Convex is asking about KMS/HSM, network isolation, and SOC2 evidence. We have VPC Private offering and KMS integration. We'll need to confirm whether they require HSM-backed keys.
darius (AE): They flagged HSM for encryption-at-rest for certain customers. Is HSM possible for Private deployments?
olivia (Security): Yes for Private we can integrate customer HSM or cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys. For Hosted we provide KMS but not customer-managed HSM unless partner arrangement. I'll attach the SOC2 cert link and answers.
elaine (SE): Operational checklist for the run: 1) model pinned to a test snapshot; 2) warm cache window; 3) metrics: p50, p95, p99, cpu/gpu utilization, token cost; 4) canary fallback to 6b if we hit degradation.
darius (AE): Can we do a canary policy that automatically routes to the 6b variant if p99 > 500ms for more than 2 minutes?
elaine (SE): Yes — we can configure threshold-based fallback. We'll run the canary during stress phase to validate behavior.
chris (SRE): I'll provision the Dedicated pool for Thu stress and ensure tracing hooks are on. Also will capture cold-start profiles (first request latency) vs warm.
darius (AE): Logistics: Convex prefers Wed-Thu window next week (local PST). Can we lock Wed smoke + Thu stress?
elaine (SE): Wed smoke confirmed, Thu stress confirmed. Need Convex contact and a service account for load runner.
darius (AE): I'll share contact and creds. Also ask them to sign the standard load test AUP (small doc).
olivia (Security): One blocker: Convex asked for dedicated audit logging retention 12 months — default is 90 days. We can do 12 months as an add-on; will need approval from billing for pricing.
darius (AE): Noted — I'll flag pricing add-on.
elaine (SE): After runs we'll post a results writeup: tail-latency heatmap, throughput timeline, token cost estimate, recommendation (model + quant + caching params). Plan to send draft within 24h after tests.
eval-bot: [analysis ready] Basic acceptance tests passed, scenario id: convx-2026-03-poc.
darius (AE): Great — thanks all. Next steps: I'll send Convex the schedule + AUP + service account. Elaine/Chris/Olivia please paste final run commands and security answers in this thread by EOD Mon. :thumbsup:
